name: Lateral Bound
description: The lateral bound is a unilateral plyometric exercise in which the athlete pushes off one leg to jump laterally, landing on the opposite leg and absorbing the force through a single-leg deceleration. It trains the lateral power production of the gluteus medius and abductors alongside the hip and knee stability required during single-leg landing, closely replicating the lateral change-of-direction mechanics common in court and field sports.

execution.starting_position: Stand on one leg with the opposite leg slightly raised. Slight forward lean at the hip.
execution.setup_instructions: Mark a starting point. Ensure a non-slip surface with adequate lateral space.
steps: Step 1: Balance on one leg with a slight hip hinge.
Step 2: Drive off the supporting leg laterally, extending the hip and pushing forcefully to one side.
Step 3: Land on the opposite foot, absorbing the impact through the hip, knee, and ankle.
Step 4: Pause to stabilize on the landing leg, then immediately bound in the opposite direction.
Step 5: Continue alternating for the prescribed repetitions.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on each bound takeoff. Breathe during the momentary pause between bounds.
common_mistakes: Landing with the knee caving inward (valgus collapse) — the hip must actively control alignment
Not pausing to stabilize on landing before rebounding
Pushing off with both feet — this must be a single-leg drive
safety_considerations: Single-leg landing requires good hip and knee stability — regress to split-stance jumps if unable to control the single-leg landing.
Ankle sprains risk on uneven or slippery surfaces.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Maximize lateral distance while maintaining control of the single-leg landing.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Explosive drive. Brief stable pause on landing. 6–10 bounds per set.
coaching_cues: One foot takeoff — drive to the side
Stick the landing — balance before you bound again
Knee stays over the toes on landing
